newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa sells Galeries Lafayette stake.
newsitem.headline: Axa sells Galeries Lafayette stake.

text.p: French insurer Axa has sold its holding of nearly five percent in retailer Galeries Lafayette, a spokeswoman for Axa said on Monday.

She confirmed the sale after portfolio managers said a block of 60,587 Galeries Lafayette shares, representing 4.63 percent of the retailer's capital, was traded on Monday morning at a price of 1,830 francs per share.
Axa had reduced its stake in the Galeries Lafayette to just under five percent at the end of December from 8.23 percent in September.
"It's simply a portfolio arbitrage operation and has nothing to do with the merger with UAP," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Axa announced in November that it had reached an agreement to merge with Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) to create the world's second-largest insurance group.
The French financial press reported in November that Axa was studying sales of its stakes in several companies, including Saint-Gobain, Elf, Lyonnaise des Eaux and Galeries Lafayette.
